thread:
maria chen: Heads up — during the multi-region failover replay this morning I saw repeated 40–120ms token-latency spikes when we fell back to us-west-2. Pattern looks like KV cache warmup combined with a kernel mismatch path. attaching quick summary below.

kevin o'neil: ugh. do you have a repro harness config? was it synthetic flood or replay traffic?

maria chen: replay harness with live traffic traces, but we injected synthetic failover events (region cut + reroute to fallback) every ~90s. the replay runner used our normal batching heuristics. noticed cache miss storms when the fallback node used different kernel selection (int8-quant vs fp16 path) => perf cliff.

jamal khan: can you paste the profiler output? curious whether it's kernel kernel_select() churn or the runtime stalling on KV eviction locks.

maria chen: pasted excerpt: ```
[profiler] time=00:00:12.345 kernel_select: 18.2ms
[profiler] time=00:00:12.345 kv_cache_evict_lock: 12.9ms
[profiler] time=00:00:12.346 kernel_launch: 6.1ms
[profiler] time=00:00:12.346 batch_merge: 3.2ms
```
Looks like kernel_select + kv eviction together stack.

sarah li: interesting. could be the kernel scoring policy prefers int8 when seq_len <= 128 but fallback model variant had slightly different tokenization giving longer seqs so we flip kernels. that flip invalidates the warm KV layout and we pay eviction+rebuild.

liam parker: we should run a controlled floodbench: synthetic bursts -> poisson background -> region switch at T+30s. baseline with kernel pinning and with dynamic selection. want apples-to-apples.

maria chen: exactly. proposed floodbench config snippet: ```yaml
floodbench: 
  duration_s: 300
  background_rate_qps: 50
  burst_pattern: 
    - at: 30s; qps: 1200; duration: 4s
    - every: 60s; qps: 900; duration: 3s
  replay_traces: s3://replays/us-prod-weekday-2pm
  region_switch_at: 45s
  kernel_pinning: [auto, pinned_fp16, pinned_int8]
  kv_policy: [lru, sticky-on-retry]
```

kevin o'neil: nice. add an explicit `cold-kv` run where we intentionally drop cache before region switch to isolate warmup impact. also record per-token latency p95/p99 and kernel version labels in logs.

jamal khan: for apples-to-apples we also need same batching heuristic parameters across regions (batching window, max_batch_tokens). otherwise the routing change also changes microbatching shape and confounds results.

maria chen: noted. i'll run three axes: (1) kernel_pinning vs dynamic, (2) kv_policy variants, (3) batching window from 2–20ms. each run repeated 5x.

infra-bot: floodbench run queued by maria chen: id=flood-2026-03-18-001, expected finish ~35m.

sarah li: can we also capture kernel selection traces per-request? even a single-line label like `kernel=int8` in the request trace helps correlate latency spikes.

liam parker: yes, add `kernel_hint` header and persist in trace. also log `kv_hit_ratio` per-request if possible.

kevin o'neil: if kernel_select() is expensive, consider caching kernel decisions per-model+seq_len bucket for 1s. cheap heuristic: key=(model,seq_bucket,token_type) -> kernel_id; invalidate on model variant change.

maria chen: that's a good short-term mitigation. longer term we should harmonize kernel scoring so fallback variants map to compatible kernels when possible.

jamal khan: action items?

maria chen: (1) run floodbench id flood-2026-03-18-001 and upload results to s3://bench-results/flood-2026-03-18/ (2) kevin to add cold-kv and kernel labels to trace; (3) jamal to prototype short-lived kernel decision cache; (4) sarah to audit kernel scoring thresholds for fallback model variants. i'll post run summary once infra-bot finishes.

liam parker: thanks — ping if you need extra quota for burst QPS. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: floodbench run completed: id=flood-2026-03-18-001, status=completed, artifact=s3://bench-results/flood-2026-03-18/artifact.tar.gz

maria chen: uploaded preliminary csv and p95/p99 plots. early takeaway: dynamic kernel selection + lru kv_policy has 2x p99 regressions during region switch; pinning to fp16 lowers p99 but increases mean by ~4ms. full analysis in s3.

kevin o'neil: can you share the p99 timeline? want to see aligned spikes at region_switch_at.

maria chen: shared link: https://s3.console.aws.amazon.com/s3/object/bench-results/flood-2026-03-18/p99_timeline.png

jamal khan: thanks. looks like eviction windows align with kernel flips. i'll start a prototype for the kernel decision cache today.

sarah li: i'll open a small PR to tweak scoring so int8 is only selected when both seq_len_bucket and token_entropy < 0.6 to avoid flips on borderline cases.

maria chen: cool. i'll schedule a follow-up run after those changes. thanks all.

liam parker: :rocket:
